title: The Three Questions Every Data System Has to Answer Before It Breaks
description: A system that works correctly today is not a promise. It is a snapshot. Load increases. Hardware fails. A developer changes one line of code and quietly breaks an assumption that was never written down.

title: Why Your Average Response Time Is Lying to You
description: A pizza shop hangs a sign in its window. Average delivery time, 25 minutes. Last Friday, one customer waited two hours for a cold pie. Both of those facts are true at the same time.

title: Why a Server Saying No on Purpose Can Be the Healthiest Thing It Does
description: Why intentional rejection protects overall system viability: understanding backpressure, rate-limiting, and load shedding to avoid catastrophic crashes when incoming traffic peaks.

title: Why a Poorly Scoped Circuit Breaker Can Turn a Small Failure Into a Big One
description: The anatomy of blast radiuses: how over-eager or broadly scoped circuit breakers turn localized component errors into widespread system outages, and how to scope fault boundaries properly.

title: Why Retrying a Failed Request Can Make Everything Worse
description: Exploring retry storms and metastable failure states: why intuitive client-side retries amplify backend saturation, and why simple backoff with jitter is not always enough.

title: Why One Post From a Celebrity Can Break a Database
description: The viral fan-out dilemma: how an unexpected surge in follower interactions causes database hot-partitioning, cache invalidation stampedes, and write lock contention.

title: Why the Servers You Rent and the Servers You Own Make Completely Different Promises
description: Cloud rentals vs. self-hosted bare metal: weighing operational convenience, vendor boundaries, cost predictability, and strategic control for modern engineering teams.

title: Why Your Bank App and Your Company’s Sales Report Run on Completely Different Systems
description: Breaking down transactional vs. analytical workloads: why systems of record separate from reporting engines, and how HTAP attempts to bridge the gap.

title: Route Handlers and Middleware in Next.js, Through the Eyes of an Express Developer
description: Bridging the paradigm shift between Express middleware pipelines and Next.js App Router route handlers, edge runtimes, and request context handling.

title: Next.js Routing Deep Dive: Parallel Routes & Intercepting Routes
description: Mastering advanced routing mechanisms in Next.js: building modal workflows, contextual routing slots, and multi-view layouts without losing URL integrity.

title: Next.js Routing and Rendering, In Plain Simple Terms
description: A clear, visual breakdown of Server Components, Client Components, Static Site Generation (SSG), and Dynamic Rendering without confusing terminology.

title: Renders, Memoization, and Refs: Everything I Learned Prepping for React Interviews
description: Comprehensive deep dive into React reconciliation, render passes, useMemo, useCallback trade-offs, and mutable ref values under the hood.

title: JavaScript’s Hidden Engine: How the Event Loop, Memory, and Garbage Collection Actually Work
description: An in-depth look under the hood of JavaScript runtimes: microtask queues, macrotasks, stack frames, heap allocation, and mark-and-sweep garbage collection.

title: I Spent a Weekend Learning How Software Actually Gets from Your Laptop to Millions of Users
description: Unpacking CI/CD pipelines, containerization, reverse proxies, CDNs, and orchestration from a developer perspective stepping into infrastructure.

title: How JavaScript Actually Works: Engines, V8, and the Code Behind Your Code
description: From source code to machine instructions: JIT compilation, Ignition bytecode interpreter, TurboFan optimization passes, and hidden classes in V8.
